label: DRAFT FIELD BRIEF FOR TECHNICIAN CONFIRMATION

sources.title: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, section 2
sources.banner: The page said section 2 is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 7 November 2026. It also said revised legislation on the site may not be fully up to date.
sources.taken: Section 2(1): it shall be the duty of every employer to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, the health, safety and welfare at work of all his employees. Section 2(2)(a) includes plant and systems of work that are, so far as is reasonably practicable, safe and without risks to health. Section 2(2)(c) includes information, instruction, training and supervision. Section 2(2)(d) includes, so far as is reasonably practicable, a place of work under the employer's control and safe access and egress. The provision is marked U.K. on the page. This brief does not decide that the duty was met.

sources.title: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, section 3
sources.banner: The page said section 3 is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 7 November 2026.
sources.taken: Section 3(1): it shall be the duty of every employer to conduct his undertaking in such a way as to ensure, so far as is reasonably practicable, that persons not in his employment who may be affected thereby are not thereby exposed to risks to their health or safety. The provision is marked U.K. on the page. This brief does not decide that the duty was met.

sources.title: Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, section 7
sources.banner: The page said section 7 is up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 9 November 2026.
sources.taken: Section 7: it shall be the duty of every employee while at work to take reasonable care for the health and safety of himself and of other persons who may be affected by his acts or omissions at work, and to co-operate with his employer so far as is necessary to enable a duty under the relevant statutory provisions to be performed. The provision is marked U.K. on the page. Confirming this brief is not that co-operation being performed by the agent.

sources.title: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, regulation 3
sources.banner: The regulation heading on the page is marked E+W+S. The page said there are currently no known outstanding effects for regulation 3.
sources.taken: Regulation 3(1): every employer shall make a suitable and sufficient assessment of the risks to the health and safety of his employees to which they are exposed whilst they are at work, and the risks to persons not in his employment arising out of or in connection with the conduct by him of his undertaking. This brief is not that assessment.

sources.title: Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, section 10A
sources.banner: The page listed changes yet to be applied, including substitution of section 10A(1) by the Renters' Rights Act 2025, section 60. Those amendments were not in the text that was read. Their commencement was not opened. The provision is marked E+W.
sources.taken: Section 10A(1) applies to a lease of a dwelling in England that is a relevant social housing lease, where section 9A applies or would apply but for section 9B(3). Section 10A(2) implies a covenant by the lessor to comply with all prescribed requirements applicable to that lease. Section 10A(3) requires regulations for action on prescribed hazards within the periods the regulations specify. Section 10A(5) is a defence if the lessor proves all reasonable endeavours to avoid the breach. This brief does not decide that the covenant applies or that the defence is made out.

sources.title: Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025, regulation 1
sources.banner: The page said there are currently no known outstanding effects for regulation 1.
sources.taken: Regulation 1(2): these Regulations come into force on 27 October 2025. Regulation 1(3): they extend to England and Wales. Regulation 1(4): they apply to lessors of social homes in England (whenever the lease was granted).

sources.title: Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025, regulation 3
sources.banner: The page said there are currently no known outstanding effects for regulation 3. Commencement information on the page says regulation 3 is in force at 27 October 2025.
sources.taken: Regulation 3(1)(b): a significant risk of harm is a risk that a reasonable lessor with the relevant knowledge would take steps to make safe as a matter of urgency (but not within 24 hours). Regulation 3(1)(d): an imminent and significant risk is one that a reasonable lessor would take steps to make safe within 24 hours. For a significant hazard, regulation 3(2) limits a relevant hazard to a prescribed hazard where the risk is associated with exposure to damp, mould or fungal growth. For an emergency hazard, the risk is not associated with a lack of adequate space for living and sleeping. This brief does not apply that test. Experiment 05 may illustrate a clock. Officer approval is not passed, so the illustration is not operative.

sources.title: UK GDPR, Article 5
sources.banner: Opened on 10 November 2026. Article 5(3) and the Article 5(1) amendments are on the page.
sources.taken: Article 5(1)(c) is data minimisation: adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary. Article 5(1)(d) is accuracy. Article 5(2) is accountability. This brief does not decide that a controller met Article 5.

sources.title: UK GDPR, Article 6
sources.banner: The page said there are currently no known outstanding effects by UK legislation for Article 6.
sources.taken: Article 6(1) lists the bases on which processing shall be lawful. The closing words of Article 6(1) say points (ea) and (f) shall not apply to processing carried out by public authorities in the performance of their tasks. No basis is asserted. A utility or a facilities contractor confirms its own basis. Do not copy a basis from another experiment.

sources.title: Harnesses in Copilot Studio
sources.banner: The page did not use the word preview for the three harnesses. That is not a general-availability claim for a click-path that was not exercised in a tenant.
sources.taken: The standard harness follows the topics and rules the maker defines. The GitHub Copilot harness is a Microsoft Copilot Studio authoring and orchestration framework, not the GitHub Copilot service. The page says customer data is not sent to the GitHub Copilot service when agents run in Copilot Studio. Agents on that harness use Copilot Credits. The page states no price. The billing articles were not opened.

sources_not_opened: Not opened on 10 November 2026: UK GDPR Article 9, Article 22A, the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 commencement instrument S.I. 2026/82, the Renters' Rights Act 2025 commencement for the listed section 10A amendments, Phase 2 of the hazards regulations, regulation 5 and regulation 20 of SI 2025/1042, and any FCA Handbook provision. Nothing in those pages is quoted. Whether a Phase 2 instrument has been made since Experiment 05's reading on 24 October 2026 is unverified here.
